# Canva: Pre-Meeting Briefing for 17 November 2026

*Prepared 15 November 2026. Coverage window: approximately 16 October to 15 November 2026. Items I could not verify are marked **[Unverified]**.*

## Executive Summary

Canva is in the middle of its most significant internal change in the period reviewed. On 3 November 2026 it announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, about 22% of its workforce, through job losses, role changes and relocations ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). The change merges Product, Growth and Platform into one product organisation, simplifies management layers and concentrates more product teams in Sydney ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). The stated trigger is slowing growth. My assessment is that the restructuring is primarily an operating-model change aimed at faster product delivery, but it is being pursued under visible financial pressure. The growth slowdown, not the headcount figure, is the most material signal for the meeting.

## What Changed in the Last 30 Days

### Restructuring and Workforce

| Item | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins's note "An important update on our team" | [Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update) |
| Scale | 1,271 roles, about 22% of workforce; includes relocations, so final exits are not yet known | [Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250) |
| Org change | Product, Growth and Platform merge into one product organisation | [Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations) |
| Location | Sydney to become the primary home for more product teams and other roles | [Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250) |
| Exit terms | At least six months' salary (about 26 weeks) for departing staff | [Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations); [Srivastava, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137) |
| Timeline | Company All Hands on 10 November; Org All Hands from 11 November | [Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/newsroom/news/canva-team-update) |
| Pre-announcement reporting | Capital Brief had reported possible November cuts or a hiring freeze | [Srivastava, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137) |

Canva has not published a breakdown of the affected roles by title, department or country ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). Per a Canva spokesperson, AI is not replacing the affected roles ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). This is a company statement relayed by a third party, not a primary Canva source I could verify.

### Financial Context

- Canva is privately held and reported about US$3.5 billion in revenue for the previous year, and states it is profitable on a free cash flow basis ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)).
- Canva expects about 20% year-on-year revenue growth and says 2026 will be its tenth consecutive profitable year ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)).
- In August 2026, Canva reportedly cut its 2026 growth forecast from 30% to 20% ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). I could not access the Fortune original cited there, so treat this as secondary reporting.
- Perkins said growth had slowed for the first time in a decade and that small adjustments would not be enough ([Bashir, 2026](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/articles/canva-first-growth-slowdown-decade-092457264.html)).
- Perkins described the moment as "without doubt the hardest moment in our thirteen-year history" ([Poduval, 2026](https://uxuiopen.com/blog/canva-layoff)).

### Product Launches

- **Within the 30-day window:** I found no verified product launch dated between 16 October and 15 November 2026.
- **Recent but outside the window:** Canva announced enterprise-oriented features in May 2026, including workflow automation, data integrations and team collaboration ([Kirkpatrick, 2026](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/canvas-may-2026-launches-signal-an-enterprise-platform-ambition-beyond-design)). The September 2026 release covered websites, a PayPal app, Sheets collaboration, Whiteboards and brand kit automation ([Canva, 2026](https://www.canva.com/design-school/resources/whats-new-canva-sep26)).
- **[Unverified] Canva Create 2026 / "Canva AI 2.0":** A YouTube video references this launch ([YouTube, n.d.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qYTLCKzMYcU)), but the video page does not show a verifiable date. I could not confirm its date or contents.

### Executive and Key Hires

- **[Unverified]** I found no verified executive or key hire announcements in the window. The restructuring also reduces management layers ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)), so leadership changes are likely, but I could not confirm any named appointments or departures.

### Deals and Partnerships

- **[Unverified]** A headline lists "Canva expands design creation inside Google Gemini," but I have no source URL, publication date or details for it. I have not treated it as fact.
- I found no verified acquisitions or partnerships announced in the window.

## Analysis

**Opinion:** The restructuring is best read as an attempt to shorten the time between insight and shipped product. Niehues argues that the delay comes from handovers, since each improvement had to be agreed between Product, Growth and Platform ([Niehues, 2026](https://www.niehuesconsulting.de/en/blog/canva-restructuring-lessons-for-organisations)). A growth leader on LinkedIn makes a similar point, arguing that AI-driven competition makes separate teams a cost ([LinkedIn, n.d.](https://www.linkedin.com/news/story/canva-announces-restructuring-affecting-over-1200-jobs-7754140)). This view is credible, but it is not independently verified and comes from practitioners rather than Canva.

Canva's framing as a simplification rather than a cost cut is plausible given continued profitability ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)). However, a 10-point cut in growth guidance, the reported consideration of a hiring freeze ([Srivastava, 2026](https://www.peoplematters.in/news/strategic-hr/canva-layoffs-in-november-company-reportedly-weighs-job-cuts-or-hiring-freeze-53137)), and a 26-week exit package together point to both productivity and cost discipline. The generous exit terms are also a retention and reputational tool. Commentators have praised them ([Greenwood, 2026](https://www.newsweek.com/canva-exit-package-praised-tech-company-announces-layoffs-12662250)).

The key risk is execution. Merging three large units during a 10–11 November communication cycle, with relocations to Sydney and an undisclosed exit count, creates uncertainty in product roadmaps and enterprise customer confidence. The enterprise push from May 2026 ([Kirkpatrick, 2026](https://futurumgroup.com/insights/canvas-may-2026-launches-signal-an-enterprise-platform-ambition-beyond-design)) makes that uncertainty more consequential.

## Three Open Questions for Canva

1. **Workforce outcome:** Of the 1,271 affected roles, how many will be exits, role changes and relocations, and when will the final figures be known? How many roles in the merged product organisation are in Sydney, and what relocation terms and deadlines apply?

2. **Operating model:** Which decision rights and metrics will the single product organisation use to show that handover delays have fallen? What will change in the roadmap and release cadence over the next two quarters?

3. **Growth and investment:** With 2026 growth guided to about 20% after the earlier cut, what are the priorities for enterprise workflow, integrations and AI platform investment? Is the hiring freeze in effect, and if so, which functions does it cover?

Chris G | VC + Startups on Instagram: "Canva’s 2026 layoffs have a plot twist: the company is helping its former employees become entrepreneurs.

Imagine getting laid off and your employer offers to help fund your next startup. That’s essentially what Canva is doing.

CEO Melanie Perkins announced a restructuring affecting 1,271 employees, or 22% of the workforce. Not all are being laid off; some face role changes or relocation.

But look at the exit package:

→ At least 6 months of salary
→ 12 months of healthcare where available
→ Employees keep their MacBooks
→ $10,000 startup grants through the Canva Collective Fund, with no equity taken
→ Career coaching and LinkedIn Premium

Now here’s what investors should actually pay attention to.

Canva lowered its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20% as AI costs put pressure on its business model.

Meanwhile, Product, Growth, and Platform are being consolidated into one organization.

Translation: AI isn’t just changing what software companies sell. It’s changing the cost of delivering their products and how teams need to operate.

And here’s the overlooked opportunity: Canva’s departing talent could become the next generation of startup founders.

Losing your job is never easy. But giving employees financial runway, healthcare, and a chance to build something new is a much better exit than simply handing them a severance check.

The lesson for founders? How you treat employees on the way out says a lot about how you build a company.

Would you rather have six months of severance or a shot at funding your own startup?
